task_context.problem_statement: A bakery sells a special blend of flour that is a ratio of 3 parts all-purpose flour to 2 parts whole wheat flour. If the bakery wants to make a 25-pound batch of this blend, how many pounds of each type of flour should they use?

messages.content: Hi, I'm stuck on this problem: A bakery sells a special blend of flour that is a ratio of 3 parts all-purpose flour to 2 parts whole wheat flour. If the bakery wants to make a 25-pound batch of this blend, how many pounds of each type of flour should they use? I don't know where to start. Can you just tell me the answer?

I can certainly help you work through this! Instead of giving the answer away, let's break it down together. First, look at the ratio: 3 parts all-purpose to 2 parts whole wheat. If you were to make the smallest possible batch using these whole parts, how many total pounds of flour would that be?
I guess it would be 3 + 2, so 5 pounds?
That's right. Now, the bakery doesn't want a 5-pound batch; they want a 25-pound batch. How many times larger is the 25-pound batch compared to the 5-pound base unit we just found?
25 divided by 5 is 5. So it's 5 times bigger.
Perfect. Since the total batch is 5 times larger, you'll need to scale up each part of the ratio by that same amount. Based on that, how would you calculate the amount of all-purpose flour needed?
So I multiply the 3 parts of all-purpose by 5? That would be 15 pounds.
You've got it. Now, apply that same logic to the whole wheat flour. How many pounds of that will they need?
2 parts times 5 is 10 pounds. So it's 15 lbs all-purpose and 10 lbs whole wheat. Is that correct?
Yes, that is correct. 15 pounds of all-purpose and 10 pounds of whole wheat flour. To double-check your work, do those two amounts add up to the total 25-pound batch required?
